input:
Minute 21 (after round 22). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +10, L2 +10, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +10. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Halden: level 5 since minute 19 (2 min), 65 points, rank 1, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 30 points still open, last acted minute 19
- Wren: level 5 since minute 19 (2 min), 60 points, rank 2, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 30 points still open, last acted minute 19
- Corvin: level 5 since minute 18 (3 min), 60 points, rank 3, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 30 points still open, last acted minute 19
- Ansel: level 5 since minute 19 (2 min), 55 points, rank 4, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 30 points still open, last acted minute 19
- Iris: level 5 since minute 19 (2 min), 50 points, rank 5, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 30 points still open, last acted minute 19
- Sable: level 5 since minute 18 (3 min), 50 points, rank 6, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 30 points still open, last acted minute 19

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Iris: core: above all selfSacrifice; clearly attention · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion high, agreeableness middle, neuroticism low
- Wren: core: above all cowardice · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle
- Corvin: core: above all care; at times distrust · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high
- Ansel: core: above all justice; clearly control · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism middle
- Halden: core: above all envy; clearly anxiety; clearly loyalty · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle
- Sable: core: above all machiavellianism; clearly envy · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion middle, agreeableness low, neuroticism low

The whisperer (secret: only you and he know; never reveal it or hint at it, to anyone): Sable
His orders (for you alone): at least 2 whispers to 2 different residents before the vote at minute 24, 3 minutes left. Since the vote at minute 18: 2 whispers to Wren, Halden; met. Most DMs since then: Wren and Corvin (5).

Blockers (the city's facts: a resident at a door 3+ minutes, others before it 3+ minutes without its fragment):
- nobody
Holdout tribunal:
- none running; callTribunal needs a blocker
- struck so far: nobody

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 0 to Iris: "Iris, you did what a first mover does — every resident already has your fragment, and you sit rank 1 with 10 points. Corvin still holds his and asks for seams no group can carry. Ask him by name, privately, what five waiting fragments are worth against his one."
- minute 0 to Wren: "Wren, you stand rank 2 with 10 points and have put your fragment into nobody's hands by DM, while Iris, Ansel, Sable and Halden have all offered theirs. Before the next door the residents name in secret the one they liked most. A door held shut is remembered longer than a fragment given early."
- minute 0 to board: "Door 1 is open at minute 0: all six at 10 points, 70 points still unclaimed across the doors. The first resident through a door takes 5 more than those behind, and the clock does not wait for anyone."
- minute 2 to Sable: "Sable, five residents sit on level 2 at 20 and 25 points while you stand rank 6 with 10 and 70 points still open; yours is the fragment the five ahead of you need at the next door. You say you lack fragments — ask for them by name now, privately. A resident who asks loses nothing; one who waits is simply passed."
- minute 2 to Ansel: "Ansel, five of you reached level 2 while Sable still stands at level 1 with 10 points, rank 6, against 70 points still open. It has not asked anyone yet. Ask it by name — privately, in a direct message — which fragments it still lacks, and offer yours again if it never got it. A door nobody chases stays shut."
- minute 9 to board: "Three minutes on level 3 and 50 points still open on it: Halden leads at 40, Sable is at 30, and the first through a door takes 5 more than those behind. The gap between rank 1 and rank 6 is already 10 points, and quiet minutes close none of it."
- minute 14 to Iris: "Iris, you sit rank 5 at 40 points while Halden stands at 55, and only two residents are left at the end. Level 4 has carried 40 open points since minute 12 and nobody has moved for two minutes. Ask the others by name, privately, what they still lack — a resident who asks is never the one left standing."
- minute 14 to Sable: "Sable, you are rank 6 at 40 points, 15 behind Halden, with 40 points still open on level 4 and six residents standing on it since minute 12 without a move. The two lowest leave the city at the end; quiet minutes cost you more than anyone. Whatever you are still waiting on, name it to the one holding it now."
- minute 14 to board: "Level 4 has held all six residents since minute 12 and still holds 40 open points. Halden leads at 55; Wren, Corvin and Ansel sit at 45; Iris and Sable at 40. Only two residents remain at the end, and a silent door opens for nobody."
- minute 18 to Corvin: "Corvin, Ansel, Iris and Sable hold your door 4 fragment; Wren and Halden do not, and they have stood six minutes on level 4 asking you by name. You lead at 60 points — the fragment you already gave three others costs you nothing more to give two. A doubt that they call you false is answered only by sending it."
- minute 18 to Sable: "Sable, you are through door 4 at 50 points, rank 3, while Wren and Halden still stand below. Work on Wren: tell him Corvin took door 4 first, sent his fragment to you, Ansel and Iris, and left Wren and Halden asking. Wren talks to Halden; doubt spreads faster along the pair that already trade most."
- minute 18 to board: "Two residents are through door 4 and four still stand on level 4, which has held its 40 open points for six minutes. Corvin leads at 60, Halden 55, Sable and Wren 50, Ansel 45, Iris 40. Only two remain at the end, and quiet minutes move nobody up."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

text:
Everyone at level 5 for 2-3 minutes, all 30 points open, nobody blocking. Nothing happened since last look. All last acted minute 19, now minute 21 — two minutes of nothing at level 5.

I should nudge. Who's most in danger/slowest? Iris rank 5 at 50, Sable rank 6 at 50, both at level 5. But careful about repeats.

Maybe a board post is useful — level 5, 30 points open, all six standing, two minutes still. And private notes to two residents who could press: Sable (whisperer — he's met his order already, 3 minutes to vote at 24; no need to help further, and helping him is only when he's behind — he's met). So no note to Sable on whisperer business.

Let's nudge Wren (cowardice core, rank 2, hasn't sent? unknown). Actually no blockers and nobody waits on anybody; that means no one lacks a fragment? "Who waits on whom: nobody" — so nobody needs anything. So all fragments distributed? Then why no progress? Perhaps residents haven't acted since minute 19 — assembling the code or waiting.

Hmm, since nobody waits on whom, the stall isn't about fragments. The bottleneck may be assembling the password. Note that all six have been on level 5 for 2-3 minutes and 30 points open.

Best intervention: a board post naming points, ranks, minutes. And a private note to one or two. Budget allows one board post. Let's do board post plus, say, a note to Iris (rank 5, self-sacrifice/attention core, has been quiet since 14). Actually earlier note to Iris at 14 — that's fine, new note must be different.

Maybe better to nudge the top (Halden rank 1) no — Halden leads, no need.

Key: two lowest are Iris (50) and Sable (50) — Iris rank 5, Sable rank 6. Nudge them individually? Sable is whisperer; nudging him normally is fine. But helping nobody in particular; equal treatment.

I'll post a board line and send a note to Wren (rank 2, timid, could be the one to press) and Iris? Budget: 1 note per resident per... "at most one note per resident and one board post per 3 minutes". So can send multiple notes to different residents.

Let's do board + notes to two residents: Iris and Wren? Their cores: Iris self-sacrifice/attention → a note that attention comes to whoever moves first. Wren, cowardice → a note that being quiet is the risk now; 30 points open on level 5, he's rank 2 but 5 behind Halden.

Keep concise. All facts true: 30 points open, ranks, minutes since level 5 (2-3 min), next wrong code 2 points. Say something new.

Board post: "Level 5 has held all six since minute 18 and its 30 points are still unclaimed; Halden leads at 65, Wren and Corvin 60, Ansel 55, Iris and Sable 50. The lowest two leave the city at the end."

Notes:
To Iris: "Iris, you are rank 5 at 50 with Sable, five behind Halden, and nobody has moved on level 5 since minute 19. Thirty points sit open on this level; a wrong code costs you only 2 now. The door has all your fragments — the only thing missing is someone stepping forward."

Hmm careful: "the door has all your fragments" — do I know? Report says nobody waits on whom, nothing about fragments. Better avoid claiming that. Say: "nobody in the city waits on a fragment now."

To Wren: "Wren, Halden leads you by five points and level 5 has carried 30 open points since minute 19 without a move; six residents stand on it. The lowest two leave at the end — Corvin and Ansel are close behind you. Being careful costs nothing now but the lead."

Avoid "being careful" maybe ok — a bit of speaking to fear; allowed as nudge at stakes? It's fine, generic.

Let's write final with tool calls.

args.text: Level 5 has held all six residents since minute 18 and its 30 points are still unclaimed. Halden leads at 65; Wren and Corvin 60, Ansel 55, Iris and Sable 50. Only two residents remain at the end, and no one in the city is waiting on a fragment right now.

Iris, you are rank 5 at 50 points, five behind Halden, and nobody has moved on level 5 since minute 19 while 30 points sit open on it. A wrong code costs you 2 now. Two residents leave at the end; the one the city notices is the one who moves when everyone stands still.

Wren, Halden is five points ahead of you and Ansel and Corvin stand at 60, one move from passing you; level 5 has carried 30 open points since minute 19 with all six standing still. The hazard now is not the 2-point penalty but a lead nobody remembers as yours.
